label: Cognitivist explanations remain rivals to Blackburn's claimed supervenience advantage
paraphrase: Van Roojen's comparative objection is that reductive naturalists can reject the premise of no analytic natural-to-moral entailment, anti-Humean cognitivists can treat beliefs as action-guiding, and cognitivists can acknowledge analyticity as a competence requirement. The existence of these replies prevents the supervenience datum by itself from establishing a special explanatory advantage for non-cognitivism; the replies' adequacy is still open.
